items.name: Readability
items.evidence: reconcileQueryState has clear names and numbered section comments ("// 1. Data freshness"). But the marker is set twice (a Symbol.for key plus `__persisterRestoreResult`), and the QueryPersister union `T | PersisterRestoreResult<T, any> | PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>` repeats itself and is hard to read.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: reconcileQueryState is one function of about 98 lines (persister.ts L46-144) that handles data, error, status and invalidation together. The bulk path still builds queries inline with `{...persistedQuery.state, fetchStatus:'idle'}` instead of going through one shared restore helper. Public types use any-casts.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The persisted state is a Partial<QueryState> that is never normalised: counts and timestamps are not validated, only defaulted with `?? 0`. `(value as any).__persisterRestoreResult` accepts any object carrying that flag. Errors are not swallowed, and hidden tests pass.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult is exported and its tests show no onSuccess/onSettled calls and fetchStatus idle. However, isPersisterRestoreResult also accepts a plain duck-typed `__persisterRestoreResult` property, so the marker can be forged. data/state are both optional, and the bulk path does not clearly share one restore path.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: The new exports are additive and the createPersister options look unchanged. But the public QueryPersister type was widened with `PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>`, and createPersister.ts internals changed (88 lines), which may shift how the plain-data path behaves. Existing tests still pass.
